lessons.title: Can, prepositions of place and imperatives

theory.en:
## *Can* and *can't*

Use **can** for ability (*I can swim*) and for possibility or permission (*You can park here*).

| | Example |
|---|---|
| + | *I / you / he / she / we / they **can** swim.* |
| − | *She **can't** (cannot) drive.* |
| ? | ***Can** you cook?* — *Yes, I **can**.* / *No, I **can't**.* |

- *Can* is the same for every person: *he **can*** (not *he cans*).
- After *can*, use the **base verb** with no *to*: *I can **play*** (not *I can to play*, *I can plays*).

## Prepositions of place

| Preposition | Example |
|---|---|
| **in** | *The keys are **in** my bag.* |
| **on** | *The phone is **on** the table.* |
| **under** | *The cat is **under** the bed.* |
| **next to** | *The bank is **next to** the café.* |
| **between** | *The pharmacy is **between** the bank and the hotel.* |
| **across from** | *The park is **across from** the school.* (on the other side of the street) |
| **behind** | *The yard is **behind** the house.* |
| **in front of** | *The bus stop is **in front of** the museum.* |

With streets, use **on**: *The library is **on** Park Avenue.* With corners, use **on the corner of**.

## Imperatives

Use the **base verb** to give instructions, directions and advice:

- ***Turn** left. **Go** straight. **Take** the bus.*
- Negative: **Don't** + verb: ***Don't** park here. **Don't** feed the ducks.*
- Add *please* to be polite: ***Please** close the door.*
theory.es:
## *Can* y *can't*

Usa **can** (poder, saber) para hablar de habilidades (*I can swim*, sé nadar) y de posibilidad o permiso (*You can park here*, puedes estacionar aquí).

| | Ejemplo |
|---|---|
| + | *I / you / he / she / we / they **can** swim.* |
| − | *She **can't** (cannot) drive.* (No sabe manejar.) |
| ? | ***Can** you cook?* (¿Sabes cocinar?) — *Yes, I **can**.* / *No, I **can't**.* |

- *Can* es igual para todas las personas: *he **can*** (no *he cans*).
- Después de *can* va el **verbo base** sin *to*: *I can **play*** (no *I can to play* ni *I can plays*).

## Preposiciones de lugar

| Preposición | Ejemplo |
|---|---|
| **in** (en, dentro de) | *The keys are **in** my bag.* (Las llaves están en mi bolsa.) |
| **on** (en, sobre) | *The phone is **on** the table.* (El teléfono está sobre la mesa.) |
| **under** (debajo de) | *The cat is **under** the bed.* (El gato está debajo de la cama.) |
| **next to** (al lado de) | *The bank is **next to** the café.* |
| **between** (entre) | *The pharmacy is **between** the bank and the hotel.* |
| **across from** (enfrente de) | *The park is **across from** the school.* (al otro lado de la calle) |
| **behind** (detrás de) | *The yard is **behind** the house.* |
| **in front of** (delante de) | *The bus stop is **in front of** the museum.* |

Con calles se usa **on**: *The library is **on** Park Avenue.* (La biblioteca está en Park Avenue.) Con esquinas, **on the corner of**.

## Imperativos

Usa el **verbo base** para dar instrucciones, direcciones y consejos:

- ***Turn** left.* (Gira a la izquierda.) ***Go** straight.* (Sigue derecho.) ***Take** the bus.* (Toma el autobús.)
- Negativo: **Don't** + verbo: ***Don't** park here.* (No estaciones aquí.) ***Don't** feed the ducks.* (No alimentes a los patos.)
- Agrega *please* para ser amable: ***Please** close the door.*

El imperativo en inglés es igual para *tú*, *usted* y *ustedes*.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: "I ___ swim. I always stay out of the water."

explanation.en: The person stays out of the water, so they **can't** swim. The negative of *can* is *can't* (not *don't can*).
explanation.es: La persona no se mete al agua, así que **can't** swim (no sabe nadar). La negación de *can* es *can't* (no *don't can*).

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct words: "My sister can ___ the guitar."

explanation.en: After *can*, use the base verb with no *-s* and no *to*: *can play*.
explanation.es: Después de *can* va el verbo base, sin *-s* y sin *to*: *can play*.

exercises.prompt: Match each preposition with its Spanish meaning.

explanation.en: *Across from* is on the other side of the street; *in front of* is directly before something.
explanation.es: *Across from* es al otro lado de la calle (enfrente); *in front of* es justo delante de algo.

exercises.prompt: Complete with can or can't.

content.text: Fish {{g1}} swim, but they {{g2}} walk. Birds {{g3}} fly.

explanation.en: Fish **can** swim but **can't** walk; birds **can** fly.
explanation.es: Los peces **can** swim (pueden nadar) pero **can't** walk (no pueden caminar); los pájaros **can** fly (pueden volar).

exercises.prompt: "___ you speak French?" — "Yes, I can."

explanation.en: The answer *Yes, I can* tells you the question starts with **Can**.
explanation.es: La respuesta *Yes, I can* te dice que la pregunta empieza con **Can**.

exercises.prompt: Complete with on, under or between.

content.text: The phone is {{g1}} the table, on top. The cat is {{g2}} the chair, below it. The bank is {{g3}} the café and the pharmacy.

explanation.en: On top → **on**; below → **under**; in the middle of two things → **between**.
explanation.es: Encima → **on**; abajo → **under**; en medio de dos cosas → **between**.

exercises.prompt: You leave the hotel and see the bank on the other side of the street. The bank is ___ the hotel.

explanation.en: On the other side of the street = **across from**.
explanation.es: Al otro lado de la calle = **across from** (enfrente de).

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with the right instruction.

left.text: Photos aren't allowed in the museum.
The class starts in two minutes!

explanation.en: Imperatives start with the verb: *Close…*, *Open…*, *Be…*, *Hurry up!*; the negative starts with *Don't*.
explanation.es: Los imperativos empiezan con el verbo: *Close…* (cierra), *Open…* (abre), *Be quiet* (haz silencio), *Hurry up!* (¡apúrate!); el negativo empieza con *Don't*.

exercises.prompt: Complete the signs with an imperative. Use the verb in brackets.

content.text: At the pool: {{g1}} (not run)! At the corner: {{g2}} (turn) right for the bank.

explanation.en: Negative imperative: **Don't** + verb (*Don't run!*); affirmative: just the verb (*Turn right*).
explanation.es: Imperativo negativo: **Don't** + verbo (*Don't run!*, ¡no corras!); afirmativo: solo el verbo (*Turn right*, gira a la derecha).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.

explanation.en: *Can* + subject + base verb: *Can you ride a bike?*
explanation.es: *Can* + sujeto + verbo base: *Can you ride a bike?* (¿Sabes andar en bicicleta?)

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

explanation.en: Thing + *be* + preposition + place: *The library is next to the park.*
explanation.es: Cosa + *be* + preposición + lugar: *The library is next to the park.* (La biblioteca está al lado del parque.)

exercises.prompt: Say the same thing. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: I know how to cook pasta.

explanation.en: *Know how to* + verb = *can* + verb: *I can cook pasta.*
explanation.es: *Know how to* + verbo (saber hacer algo) = *can* + verbo: *I can cook pasta.*

theory.en:
## Places in town

| Place | What you do there |
|---|---|
| **bank** | get money |
| **post office** | send letters and packages |
| **supermarket** | buy food |
| **pharmacy** | buy medicine |
| **hospital** | see a doctor when you are very sick |
| **library** | read and borrow books |
| **museum** | see art and old objects |
| **movie theater** | watch movies |
| **train station** / **bus stop** | take a train / a bus |
| **hotel** | stay for a night or more |
| **park** | walk, play, relax |

## In the street

- A **street** has two sides. A **block** is the part of a street between two corners: *Walk two blocks.*
- At a **corner**, two streets meet. **Traffic lights** are red, yellow and green.
- A **map** shows you where places are.

## Asking for and giving directions

| Ask | Answer |
|---|---|
| ***Excuse me,** where's the bank?* | *It's on Main Street, next to the café.* |
| *Is there a pharmacy near here?* | *Yes, there's one on the corner.* |
| *How do I get to the museum?* | ***Go straight** for two blocks. **Turn left** at the traffic lights. It's **on your right**.* |

Say ***Thank you!*** — the answer is ***You're welcome.***
theory.es:
## Lugares de la ciudad

| Lugar | Qué haces allí |
|---|---|
| **bank** (banco) | sacar dinero |
| **post office** (oficina de correos) | enviar cartas y paquetes |
| **supermarket** (supermercado) | comprar comida |
| **pharmacy** (farmacia) | comprar medicinas |
| **hospital** | ver a un médico cuando estás muy enfermo |
| **library** (biblioteca) | leer y pedir libros prestados |
| **museum** (museo) | ver arte y objetos antiguos |
| **movie theater** (cine) | ver películas |
| **train station** / **bus stop** (estación de tren / parada de autobús) | tomar el tren / el autobús |
| **hotel** | quedarte una noche o más |
| **park** (parque) | caminar, jugar, descansar |

Cuidado: *library* es biblioteca, no librería (*bookstore*).

## En la calle

- Una **street** (calle) tiene dos lados. Un **block** (cuadra) es la parte de una calle entre dos esquinas: *Walk two blocks.* (Camina dos cuadras.)
- En una **corner** (esquina) se encuentran dos calles. Los **traffic lights** (semáforo) son rojo, amarillo y verde.
- Un **map** (mapa) te muestra dónde están los lugares.

## Pedir y dar direcciones

| Preguntar | Responder |
|---|---|
| ***Excuse me,** where's the bank?* (Disculpe, ¿dónde está el banco?) | *It's on Main Street, next to the café.* |
| *Is there a pharmacy near here?* (¿Hay una farmacia cerca?) | *Yes, there's one on the corner.* |
| *How do I get to the museum?* (¿Cómo llego al museo?) | ***Go straight** for two blocks.* (Sigue derecho dos cuadras.) ***Turn left** at the traffic lights.* (Gira a la izquierda en el semáforo.) *It's **on your right**.* (Está a tu derecha.) |

Di ***Thank you!*** — la respuesta es ***You're welcome.*** (De nada.)

theory.en:
## Reading a town guide

Town guides for visitors are divided into **sections** with headings (*Food*, *Culture*, *Parks*). Each section tells you:

| Information | Example |
|---|---|
| what there is | *There's a bank, a post office and a big supermarket.* |
| where it is | *The museum is on Park Avenue, next to the library.* |
| what you can and can't do | *You can rent a bike. You can't take photos inside.* |
| opening times and prices | *open every day from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.*, *breakfast for $9* |
| advice | *Try Rosie's Diner. Please don't feed the ducks!* |

### Tips

- Use the headings to find the right section quickly.
- To find **where** something is, look for prepositions: *next to, across from, behind, between, on the corner of*.
- **Imperatives** give advice: *Try…, Turn left…, Don't…*
- *The heart of the town* means the center, the most important part.
theory.es:
## Leer una guía de la ciudad

Las guías para visitantes están divididas en **secciones** con títulos (*Food*, *Culture*, *Parks*). Cada sección te dice:

| Información | Ejemplo |
|---|---|
| qué hay | *There's a bank, a post office and a big supermarket.* |
| dónde está | *The museum is on Park Avenue, next to the library.* |
| qué puedes y no puedes hacer | *You can rent a bike.* (Puedes alquilar una bicicleta.) *You can't take photos inside.* (No puedes tomar fotos adentro.) |
| horarios y precios | *open every day from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.*, *breakfast for $9* |
| consejos | *Try Rosie's Diner.* (Prueba Rosie's Diner.) *Please don't feed the ducks!* (¡Por favor no alimentes a los patos!) |

### Consejos

- Usa los títulos para encontrar rápido la sección correcta.
- Para saber **dónde** está algo, busca preposiciones: *next to, across from, behind, between, on the corner of*.
- Los **imperativos** dan consejos: *Try…, Turn left…, Don't…*
- *The heart of the town* (el corazón del pueblo) significa el centro, la parte más importante.
- Un *diner* es un restaurante sencillo y típico de Estados Unidos.

theory.en:
## Giving directions

Good directions are short and in order. Use imperatives and give **landmarks** (places that are easy to see):

1. **Start:** *OK. From here, go straight for two blocks.*
2. **Turns:** *Turn left at the traffic lights. Then turn right on Park Avenue.*
3. **Arrival:** *The museum is on your left, next to the library. You can't miss it!*

### Useful phrases

| To say | Example |
|---|---|
| direction | *Go straight. Turn left / right.* |
| where to turn | *at the corner, at the traffic lights, at the bank* |
| distance | *for two blocks, about five minutes on foot* |
| the place | *It's on your left / right. It's across from the park.* |

### Asking for directions

- *Excuse me, is there a pharmacy near here?*
- *How do I get to the train station?*
- *Can I walk there?* — *Yes, you can. It's about ten minutes.*
- *Thank you!* — *You're welcome.*

### Sounding natural

Check that the other person understands: *OK? Do you see the bank?* Repeat the main steps at the end: *So, straight, then left at the lights.*
theory.es:
## Dar direcciones

Unas buenas direcciones son cortas y ordenadas. Usa imperativos y da **puntos de referencia** (lugares fáciles de ver):

1. **Inicio:** *OK. From here, go straight for two blocks.* (Bueno. Desde aquí, sigue derecho dos cuadras.)
2. **Giros:** *Turn left at the traffic lights. Then turn right on Park Avenue.* (Gira a la izquierda en el semáforo. Luego gira a la derecha en Park Avenue.)
3. **Llegada:** *The museum is on your left, next to the library. You can't miss it!* (El museo está a tu izquierda, al lado de la biblioteca. ¡No tiene pérdida!)

### Frases útiles

| Para decir | Ejemplo |
|---|---|
| dirección | *Go straight. Turn left / right.* |
| dónde girar | *at the corner, at the traffic lights, at the bank* (en la esquina, en el semáforo, en el banco) |
| distancia | *for two blocks, about five minutes on foot* (dos cuadras, unos cinco minutos a pie) |
| el lugar | *It's on your left / right. It's across from the park.* |

### Pedir direcciones

- *Excuse me, is there a pharmacy near here?* (Disculpe, ¿hay una farmacia cerca?)
- *How do I get to the train station?* (¿Cómo llego a la estación de tren?)
- *Can I walk there?* (¿Puedo ir caminando?) — *Yes, you can. It's about ten minutes.*
- *Thank you!* — *You're welcome.* (De nada.)

### Sonar natural

Comprueba que la otra persona entiende: *OK? Do you see the bank?* (¿Ves el banco?) Repite los pasos principales al final: *So, straight, then left at the lights.* (Entonces, derecho y luego a la izquierda en el semáforo.)

exercises.prompt: "___ I park here?" — "No, you can't. Park on the next street."

explanation.en: We ask for permission with **Can I…?**; the answer *No, you can't* confirms it.
explanation.es: Pedimos permiso con **Can I…?** (¿Puedo…?); la respuesta *No, you can't* lo confirma.

Go straight and turn left at the lights.
Yes, you can. It's only five minutes.

explanation.en: *Where's…?* → a place; *Is there…?* → *Yes, there's one*; *Can I…?* → *Yes, you can*; *How do I get to…?* → directions; *Thank you* → *You're welcome*.
explanation.es: *Where's…?* → un lugar; *Is there…?* → *Yes, there's one*; *Can I…?* → *Yes, you can*; *How do I get to…?* → direcciones; *Thank you* → *You're welcome*.

exercises.prompt: Complete the directions.

content.text: From the hotel, {{g1}} straight for two blocks. Then {{g2}} right at the traffic lights. The museum is {{g3}} your left.

explanation.en: *go straight*, *turn right*, *on your left*.
explanation.es: *go straight* (sigue derecho), *turn right* (gira a la derecha), *on your left* (a tu izquierda).

exercises.prompt: Complete with is, are or isn't.

content.text: There {{g1}} a big park in my town, and there {{g2}} two museums. There {{g3}} a train station: we only have buses.

explanation.en: *A big park* → **is**; *two museums* → **are**; no train station → **isn't**.
explanation.es: *A big park* → **is**; *two museums* → **are**; no hay estación de tren → **isn't**.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a direction.

explanation.en: Imperative + direction + *at* + landmark: *Turn right at the bank.*
explanation.es: Imperativo + dirección + *at* + punto de referencia: *Turn right at the bank.* (Gira a la derecha en el banco.)

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.

explanation.en: *Is there a* + place + *near here?*
explanation.es: *Is there a* + lugar + *near here?* (¿Hay un hotel cerca?)

exercises.prompt: Say the same thing. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: The museum and the library are side by side.

accepted: The museum is next to the library.
The library is next to the museum.

explanation.en: *Side by side* = *next to*: *The museum is next to the library.*
explanation.es: *Side by side* (uno al lado del otro) = *next to*: *The museum is next to the library.*

exercises.prompt: Write the rule as an instruction. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: Walking on the grass is not OK.

explanation.en: Negative imperative: *Don't* + verb: *Don't walk on the grass.*
explanation.es: Imperativo negativo: *Don't* + verbo: *Don't walk on the grass.* (No pises el césped.)

exercises.prompt: A tourist says: "Thank you very much!" What do you say?

explanation.en: The answer to *Thank you* is **You're welcome**.
explanation.es: La respuesta a *Thank you* es **You're welcome** (de nada).

exercises.prompt: Give directions to your favorite place.

content.task: A new neighbor asks you how to get from your home to your favorite place in town (a café, a park, a store…). Record the directions (about 45 seconds). Say what the place is, give the directions step by step with at least two turns and landmarks, and say where the place is when they arrive.

description.en: I named the place and gave clear directions in order, with at least two turns and landmarks.
description.es: Dije el lugar y di direcciones claras y en orden, con al menos dos giros y puntos de referencia.

description.en: I used imperatives (go, turn, don't…) and prepositions of place correctly.
description.es: Usé bien los imperativos (go, turn, don't…) y las preposiciones de lugar.

description.en: I spoke clearly, checked understanding or repeated the main steps.
description.es: Hablé con claridad, comprobé que me entendían o repetí los pasos principales.

solution.model_answer: My favorite place is Café Luna. It's easy! From our building, turn right and go straight for three blocks. At the traffic lights, turn left. That's Oak Street. Walk one more block. The café is on your right, across from the library. It has a red door. You can't miss it! So: right, three blocks, then left at the lights.

exercises.prompt: Ask for directions as a visitor.

content.task: You're a visitor in Brookfield and you want to go to the museum. Record what you say to a person in the street: start politely, ask if the museum is near, ask how to get there and if you can walk, repeat the directions to check, and say thank you.

description.en: I asked at least three questions (Is there…? How do I get to…? Can I…?).
description.es: Hice al menos tres preguntas (Is there…? How do I get to…? Can I…?).

description.en: I started with Excuse me and ended with Thank you.
description.es: Empecé con Excuse me y terminé con Thank you.

description.en: I repeated the directions to check them.

solution.model_answer: Excuse me! Is the museum near here? ... Great. How do I get there? ... Can I walk? ... OK, so I turn left at the station, walk two blocks, and the museum is on Park Avenue, next to the library? ... Thank you very much!
